explorer.title: Know your roof before you call anyone.
explorer.intro: Tap a marker on the roof to see what goes wrong there, and the signs you can spot from the ground.

spots.label: Shingles
spots.what: Sun, wind and age dry shingles out until they curl, crack or blow off, leaving the layer underneath open to rain.
signs: Bald patches where the granules have worn off

spots.label: Flashing
spots.what: The metal strips around chimneys, walls and skylights. Most leaks start here, not in the middle of the roof.
signs: Rust or gaps around the chimney
Water stains on the ceiling near a wall

spots.label: Ridge & vents
spots.what: Without airflow, attic heat cooks shingles from underneath and pushes up cooling bills in a {{ state_name }} summer.
signs: Shingles ageing faster on one side

spots.label: Gutters
spots.what: Blocked or sagging gutters spill water down the walls, rot the fascia boards and send water toward the foundation.
signs: Water pouring over the edge in rain
Gutters pulling away from the house
Peeling paint or rot behind them

spots.label: Valleys
spots.what: Where two slopes meet, the rain from both runs down one channel. Worn or badly cut valleys are one of the most common places for a leak to start.
signs: Ceiling stains below where two roof slopes meet
Leaves and debris piling up in the valley
Cracked or lifted shingles along the valley line

spots.label: Hail damage
spots.what: Hail knocks the granules off and bruises the mat underneath. It often looks minor from the ground and isn't.
signs: Dark round marks on the shingles
Dents in vents, gutters or downspouts
A storm in the last few months

faq.q: How do I know if I need a repair or a whole new roof?
faq.a: It depends on the roof's age, how widespread the damage is and the state of the decking underneath. After the inspection we'll tell you plainly which one makes sense, and show you the photos that back it up.

faq.q: Will my insurance cover hail or storm damage?
faq.a: Many policies cover storm and hail damage, but it depends on yours, and your insurance company can tell you. We photograph and document what we find so you can send it to them.

faq.q: How long does a roof replacement take?
faq.a: Most homes take one to two days once the materials arrive. Bigger or more complex roofs can take longer, and we'll give you a timeline with your quote.

faq.q: How long does a shingle roof last in {{ state_name }}?
faq.a: Usually somewhere between 15 and 25 years, depending on the shingles, how well the attic is ventilated, and how many storms it has taken.

faq.q: My roof is leaking right now. What should I do?
faq.a: Move anything valuable out of the way, put a bucket under the drip, and call us. Please don't climb onto a wet roof yourself.
